figure: Figure 2. Representative interaction-level failures and selective recovery cases
selection_policy: Representative real scored cases selected to cover role reversal, predicate/relation swap, COCO-style plausible mismatch, spatial binding, and full grounding recovery. Cases prioritize CLIP failure/near-tie and interpretable changes under text-only prior or selective correction.

cases.why_selected: CLIP ranks the inverted caption higher, while the text-only ontology prior strongly identifies the implausible inversion.
cases.interpretation: text-only prior already flags the inversion; correction keeps the ranking on the right side
cases.caveat: The text prior is the main driver here; the selected grounding-aware recipe is not the strongest signal.

cases.why_selected: CLIP fails on a subject-object inversion; the text prior is only near-tie, while selective grounding flips the margin.
cases.interpretation: grounded support for who is on what resolves the near-tie
cases.caveat: The example is visually simple, so it is used as an interpretable structured-relation case rather than a broad claim.

cases.why_selected: The negative caption is a relation-preposition swap; CLIP and text-only prior fail, while rel-phrase selective correction recovers.
cases.interpretation: relation-phrase evidence separates 'on ground' from the swapped preposition
cases.caveat: Like many synthetic COCO negatives, the contrast is controlled but linguistically compressed.
cases.positive_caption: person puts hay on ground for a giraffe
cases.negative_caption: person puts hay in ground for a giraffe

cases.why_selected: A spatial preposition-sensitive Winoground case where CLIP and text prior fail but spatial binding changes the decision.
cases.interpretation: spatial binding is diagnostic for below/above-style ambiguity
cases.caveat: This is an exploded sample from a paired benchmark; native 2x2 interpretation can differ.
cases.positive_caption: there is someone below a table
cases.negative_caption: there is a table below someone

cases.why_selected: CLIP and slim rel/spatial variants do not recover this binding case, but full semantic grounding yields a positive margin.
cases.interpretation: attribute and role binding require broader grounding than a single slim cue
cases.caveat: The scene is visually complex; it illustrates a recoverable case, not a universal Winoground solution.
cases.positive_caption: a person without glasses pushes a person with glasses sitting in a box
cases.negative_caption: a person with glasses pushes a person without glasses sitting in a box
